Hi everyone, I'm Sanket and this presentation summarizes my analysis of predictors of confidence in social organizations using the World Value Survey, with Armenia as my focus country and all other countries pooled together as a comparison group. For question 1, the main takeaway is that the dataset is large but uneven. Table 1 right here shows us that the final file contains around 100,000 observations and 37 variables. If I turn the page we can see here, figure 1 shows us that the variables are highly concentrated while others are more spread out. Table 3 shows us that there is substantial missingness for some variables, especially the CEU. Figure 2 also shows that later years contribute more responses than earlier years. So overall, the data are useful but later, comparisons need to be interpreted carefully because the dataset is not perfectly balanced. Now for question 2a, I compared Armenia with the pooled other country group while ignoring time. I used the Wilcoxon Rank Sum test because this was a comparison between two independent groups, the variables were mostly ordinal and the group sizes were very unequal. Before I go any further, I must also add that for my data pre-processing, I used my student ID as a random seed and also I made a new column known as other so that I can put all the other countries in that one column while having Armenia stats in the Armenia column. So for question 2a, I compared Armenia with the pooled other countries and I used the Wilcoxon Rank Sum test. The variables were mostly ordinal and this helped me do the test further. Now in table 4, the p-values you can see here are very small therefore we can say that our result that Armenia is very different from the other countries is highly significant and therefore we can reject the null hypothesis. The main result in this is that Armenia differs from the pooled other group in several areas especially satisfaction, age, union confidence, press confidence, environmental confidence and a couple more. In figure 3, this helps us show that the direction of confidence and differences such as Armenia being higher in unions, press and civil service but lower in armed forces. This is mostly just for reference and it doesn't really tell us much about the difference so to speak of Armenia compared to the other countries but it's a good reference point to have. Now moving on to question 2b, I used Baer-Weiss-Pearson correlations to assess the predictive quality in Armenia. Here the predictive quality means strength of association not causation and figure 4 and table 5 show that most of Armenian correlations are weak overall so confidence is only partly predictable from the assigned attributes and the clearest Armenian result is the importance of religion in predicting confidence in churches. Now moving to question 2c, I repeated the same process again but this time I did it with the other country group. Table 8 shows that the strongest pair here is also importance of religion and confidence in churches and figure 5 shows a broader correlation pattern for other country groups. Now if I turn the page, here you can see the difference in the correlations for Armenia and the other country groups and this is where we can actually see the main underlying factor. You can see Armenia although both other countries and Armenia don't show strong correlation with factors, here you can see the difference is high therefore you see a lot of blues and reds because there's a lot of contrast in the direction which Armenia is moving and the other countries are moving. So that was my biggest finding for question 2. Now for question 3, I studied the change over time so this is where the temporal changes come in using waves instead of years because waves were a part of the data set and it was much easier to use it because Armenia again was using only 3 waves if I'm not wrong so years would be a little harder to work with and maybe not as accurate or easy to aggregate. So I used the Kruskal-Wallis test because the section compares multiple waves and the survey variables are ordinal and in unequal group sizes. Here in figure 7, it shows that Armenia and pooled other country groups do not follow an identical confidence trends over time and table 7 shows strong evidence of wave to wave change in Armenia especially for political parties and activity, professional activities, sport memberships, religious activity, happiness, life satisfaction and so on. So over time, changes were not just visual, they were definitely statistically important as you can even see by the p-values we found here, they're very small and therefore this is not by chance. Now moving on to the last part of the assignment, question 3b, I recalculated the predictor confidence correlations within each wave to see whether predictive strength changed over time and table 8 and figure 8 show that stronger Armenian relationships remain concentrated in a small group especially religion related ones. Again, importance of religion predicting confidence in churches remains the clearest pattern over time although some relationships do change in strength and across waves. So overall, my main conclusion is that Armenia differs from a pooled international pattern both in average responses and in how confidence relates to participant attributes but the predictive relationships are not strong across the board. Instead Armenia is characterized by a small number of more concentrated relationships especially around religion and other churches and sorry and confidence in churches and these patterns also change over time as well. So thank you so much for your attention.
